attention.basculer.aide: Synfus brings the character to the front by itself. Handy in combat, disorienting if you are typing somewhere else.
attention.releve.bandeau: strip y=%.0f px h=%.0f px · icon offsets:
attention.releve.sansBandeau: strip unreadable — measuring on the screen ordinate
attention.signaler.aide: The character blinks in the bar. You see where to go without being moved by force.
autorisation.aide: Reading the screen needs the “Screen Recording” permission.
barre.accessibiliteRequise: Synfus needs Accessibility access to list and activate windows
barre.autreBureau: On another desktop — click to switch to it
barre.panneauxSeulementDofus: Panels only in front of Dofus
barre.panneauxSeulementDofus.aide: Quests and treasure hunt hide when another app comes to the front, and come back with the game.
barre.zaap.aucunFavori: No favourite zaap — star them in Settings › Zaaps, or ⌘D in the palette
boss.aide: A panel over the game, one boss at a time (click its name to switch). Synfus counts turns from the fight button and reads what the mechanic needs: against Count Harebourg, the confusion announced in the fight channel or deduced from your health; against Kimbo, the state announced in the fight channel. It aims and casts nothing: it reads the screen and shows it. What it cannot read is noted with a click in the panel.
boss.attente.combat: Waiting for a fight. On the front character's turn, Synfus reads its health and the fight channel.
boss.coups.aide: Each damage line dealt in melee turns the confusion a quarter turn counterclockwise. Count them here when the confusion comes from your health or your choice.
boss.guide: Dungeon guide on Dofus pour les noobs
boss.harebourg.aide: The confusion of his spells: where to aim to hit the target.
boss.harebourg.impair: Odd turn: the Count is invulnerable, and each hit he takes teleports the attacker to the opposite side.
boss.harebourg.pair: Even turn: when hit, he moves to the attacker's opposite side; swapping places with an entity makes him vulnerable.
boss.ilyzaelle.aide: The 75% and 50% thresholds, Into the Darkness.
boss.ilyzaelle.alliee50: Hold until the end of turn %lld: the fight is won
boss.ilyzaelle.alliee75: Ally and invulnerable until the end of turn %lld: step into her glyph, +400%% damage
boss.ilyzaelle.gagnee: Both turns have passed: the fight should be won.
boss.ilyzaelle.objectif50: Bring her down to 50% of her max health
boss.ilyzaelle.objectif75: Bring her down to 75% of her max health — before turn 3 if possible
boss.ilyzaelle.rappel.critiques: 250 critical resistance: don't count on critical hits.
boss.ilyzaelle.rappel.erosion: Thresholds count on her max health: don't erode her.
boss.ilyzaelle.rappel.portail: Monsters come out of the portal every 3 turns: don't stay in line with them, nor grouped.
boss.ilyzaelle.tenebres.maintenant: Into the Darkness this turn: she pulls whoever is in line by 4 cells — take cover
boss.kimbo.aide: Even and odd states: where to stand, which elements to hit with.
boss.kimbo.attente: Hit Kimbo with Earth or Water, or with Air or Fire (even without damage), then choose the pair here — the fight channel says it too.
boss.kimbo.frappe.airFeu: He then loses his Air and Fire resistances: hit with those elements (Earth and Water: +800%)
boss.kimbo.frappe.terreEau: He then loses his Earth and Water resistances: hit with those elements (Air and Fire: +800%)
boss.kimbo.kimbo.impair: Bring Kimbo to an odd distance from the Disciple: he will start his turn there
boss.kimbo.kimbo.pair: Bring Kimbo to an even distance from the Disciple: he will start his turn there
boss.kimbo.question: The element pair that hit him last
boss.kimbo.rappel.disciple: Once Kimbo has a state, the Disciple can kill whoever stands next to him.
boss.kimbo.rappel.neutre: Neutral doesn't change the state; a new state replaces the old one.
boss.kimbo.rappel.parite: The Disciple gains 1 MP when placing his glyphs: his cells' parity changes from one turn to the next.
boss.kimbo.reste.impair.detail: from the Disciple — his glyphs go on even cells
boss.kimbo.reste.pair.detail: from the Disciple — his glyphs go on odd cells
boss.lecture.aide: While the panel shows, Synfus reads the fight button and, in a fight, the health heart and the chat of the front character. Their zones are calibrated in Screen reading.
boss.rappel.carillon: Don't start your turn in the Count's cross glyph: it kills.
boss.rappel.echec: Aiming at a cell off the map or out of line of sight is a critical failure — in melee, the turn is lost.
boss.rienLu: Nothing read yet: check the Health heart and Chat zones.
boss.source.prevision: Forecast for your next turn, health at %lld%%
boss.source.vie: Deduced from your health at turn start: %lld%%
boss.talKasha.aide: The three glyphs that make her vulnerable.
boss.talKasha.rappel.glyphes: A killed monster leaves a glyph where she revives it the next turn; it then skips its turn.
boss.talKasha.rappel.ligne: She hits through her allies: stay out of their line as well as hers.
boss.talKasha.rappel.pm: Removing her MP swaps your place with hers, once per turn.
boss.talKasha.reste: %lld more glyphs of different monsters to make her start her turn on
boss.talKasha.reste.un: %lld more glyph of another monster to make her start her turn on
boss.talKasha.vulnerable: Vulnerable: she started her turn on three glyphs
boss.tour.aide: Counted at the front character's turn starts, from its first turn, read from the fight button; correct it if a turn was missed.
boss.toxoliath.aide: The countdown to Volatile Poison, the waves, Toxmose.
boss.toxoliath.avant: Kill him before turn 6: %lld turns left
boss.toxoliath.avant.un: Kill him before turn 6: %lld turn left
boss.toxoliath.avantCombat: Volatile Poison on turn 6, waves on turns 1, 6, 11, 16 and 21: the count starts at the front character's first turn.
boss.toxoliath.poison.maintenant: Volatile Poison this turn: +2 MP, −2 AP, poison, damage taken +50%
boss.toxoliath.rappel.mort: Once the Toxoliath is dead, his poison is gone: his killer can move.
boss.toxoliath.rappel.toxmose: Under Toxmose, moving without MP (leap, teleport) is still possible; a debuff removes the poison, not for the current turn.
boss.toxoliath.rappel.venin: Saving Venom: the purple character takes 50% more damage for a turn, and heals whoever hits them.
boss.toxoliath.touche.aide: Toxmose: each MP used for two turns costs 700 poison.
boss.toxoliath.toxmose: Toxmose: spend no more MP until the end of turn %lld (700 poison per MP)
boss.vie.sansMax: Health read: %lld HP. Click the game's heart to show the percentage.
calibration.aucuneCapture: No capture for this element. Capture in 5 s, then go back to the game.
calibration.capturee: Captured %@ — draw a rectangle on it to place the area.
calibration.consigne.chasse: The hunt tracker only shows during a treasure hunt: start the capture, go back to the game, it is taken after 5 seconds.
calibration.consigne.combat: The “End turn” button only exists in combat: start the capture, go back to the game during a fight, it is taken after 5 seconds.
calibration.consigne.position: The area name and coordinates, top left of the game. Start the capture and go back to the game: it is taken after 5 seconds.
calibration.consigne.quetes: Open the game's quest tracker, on the left: start the capture, go back to the game, it is taken after 5 seconds. The area must cover the titles and their objectives.
calibration.consigne.tchat: The chat, bottom left, with the fight channel: start the capture, go back to the game, it is taken after 5 seconds. The zone must cover the last lines, without the input line.
calibration.consigne.vie: The health heart, in the middle of the bottom bar: start the capture, go back to the game, it is taken after 5 seconds. The zone must cover the heart's number, without AP or MP.
calibration.detecter.aide: Finds the zone on the capture, without drawing.
calibration.detecter.rien: Not found on this capture: capture it while the element is on screen.
calibration.essai.tchat.rien: No confusion announced in these lines
carte.interieur.aide: On an indoor map: the route leads outside, then go into the building.
carte.maj.casesSuspectes: DofusDB only returned %lld cells of the World of Twelve, the current map is kept.
carte.maj.suspecte: DofusDB only returned %lld places, the current map is kept.
chasse.aide: A floating panel: the start (your read position), a direction (buttons or arrow keys) and the clue (typed, or read on screen) give the next map from DofusDB, and its /travel is copied — through a zaap if it saves enough maps. Synfus validates nothing and sends nothing to the game: paste, walk and validate yourself. The panel takes the keyboard without leaving the game; a click in the game gives it back.
chasse.lire.aide: Reads the hunt tracker on screen and offers the recognised clues; the last one is selected. The read area is calibrated in Screen reading › Reading areas.
chasse.phorreur.suivre: Follow the direction (%@) until the Phorreur
classes.icones.aide: Each class gets its emblem from DofusDB, downloaded by Synfus and kept on this Mac. You can replace it with the image of your choice: a portrait, a screenshot, any PNG or JPEG — with “Choose…”, by drag and drop, or by dropping iop.png, cra.png… into the folder then “Reload”. Your icon always takes priority; “Remove” brings back the DofusDB one. Without an image, Synfus shows the colored chip.
classes.maj.aide: Class names and emblems: downloaded from api.dofusdb.fr at launch, then every 30 days, and kept on this Mac. A new class in the game shows up without updating Synfus; offline, Synfus recognizes classes from its built-in table.
classes.maj.suspecte: DofusDB returned only %lld classes, the current classes are kept.
classes.mentionAnkama: Some illustrations are the property of Ankama Studio and Dofus — All rights reserved.
combat.pasEncore: not read yet — switch to this character
diagnostic.accessibiliteManquanteQuarant: Accessibility permission missing — and this copy is quarantined, which will keep it from taking effect. See the General tab.
diagnostic.apercu.introuvable: preview: window not found at capture
diagnostic.attention.aide: Watches the only two signals an app sends outward: its window title and its Dock icon. Start the probe, play a fight, and see whether something moves when your turn comes. The icon → character pairing assumes the icons follow launch order: check that the right character is flagged. A bounce moves an icon away from its strip; at rest, the offsets must not move.
diagnostic.attention.appariementDouteux: One icon per Dofus process was expected: the pairing is unreliable here.
diagnostic.aucuneFenetre: No Dofus window detected. Is the game running?
diagnostic.fenetres.aide: The raw titles of the Dofus windows. If the name shown does not match your character, the client does not expose the name in its title; numbering then follows launch order, to be reordered in the Characters tab.
diagnostic.gelesAcheves.ligne: %@ (pid %lld) — no window and silent on three probes, force quit
diagnostic.lecture.aide: Reads, in the frontmost character's window, the position (area name and coordinates) and the combat state (coloured “End turn” button: their turn; grey: someone else's; absent: out of combat). One small area per reading, scaled to a fixed size; OCR only runs again when the area changed. If the game interface was moved, recalibrate the area under “Reading areas”. Requires Screen Recording.
diagnostic.position.etat.attente: Waiting: no Dofus client in front. Use “Read all”, or go back to the game.
diagnostic.position.etat.preparation: Preparing OCR (first model load, up to a few tens of seconds)…
diagnostic.position.etat.sansCoordonnees: Text read, but no coordinates: look at the area below — are the coordinates in it?
diagnostic.position.illisible: no coordinates in the text read
diagnostic.position.pasEncore: position: not read yet — switch to this character
diagnostic.position.stats: %lld OCR reads (last: %lld ms) · %lld unchanged readings skipped
diagnostic.position.toutLire.aide: Reads the position of every connected character, once. The regular pass only reads the frontmost character: while the settings are open, Synfus is in front.
diagnostic.rangement.aide: A full-screen window is never moved, and a character on another desktop is out of Accessibility's reach — switch to it, then arrange again.
donjon.conseils.aide: Dofus pour les noobs' tactical tips for this fight (in French)
donjon.entree.aide: Copy the route to the entrance %@, zaap included
equipes.glisserPourCreer: Drop a character here to create a team
fermeture.confirmation.detail: Each client is asked to quit, then forced if it stops responding. Characters in combat will lose their turn.
general.accessibilite.aide: Essential: this is what lets Synfus list Dofus windows, read the character's name and activate a client. Without it, no character shows up. System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
general.apercus.aide: A thumbnail of the character's window when hovering its chip. A character on another desktop or in full screen elsewhere can be captured, but its image may be stale: macOS does not redraw a window it is not showing.
general.barre.aide: Move the bar by grabbing the dots on its left. It never takes the keyboard: it is a game overlay.
general.barre.position: Position at the top of the screen
general.barre.reduire.aide: Emblem and key only; the name stays in the tooltip. The front character keeps its name.
general.barre.seulementDofus: Only when Dofus is in front
general.enregistrementEcran.aide: Used for window previews and screen reading (position, combat). A permission distinct from Accessibility; macOS often asks to relaunch Synfus after granting it. System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording.
general.iconeApp.aide: The one shown in the Finder and in alerts. The Dock doesn't show it: Synfus lives in the menu bar.
general.langue.aide: Auto: Synfus speaks the language of macOS. The choice takes effect on the next launch — the button relaunches Synfus.
general.quarantaine: This copy is quarantined: the Accessibility permission will have no effect
general.quarantaine.aide: It was downloaded, and macOS marks it as unverified. As long as that mark is there, checking Synfus in System Settings has no effect. Run the first command in Terminal then relaunch Synfus; the second resets the entry if Synfus had already been allowed before.
lecture.combatDerriere.aide: The fight of the characters you aren't looking at, even with Dofus in the background: their chip shows whether they are fighting and their turn countdown. Windowed only — macOS doesn't redraw a hidden full screen — and one capture per character every two seconds in a fight.
lecture.detecter.aide: One game capture: each visible element (position, chat, health heart, trackers, fight button) finds its zone. Open what you want calibrated first.
lecture.detecter.rien: Nothing recognised: go back to the game during the countdown, its interface visible.
lecture.zones.aide: Each game element is read in its own area, as fractions of the window. To calibrate it: a capture of the game while the element is shown, kept on this Mac, and a rectangle drawn on it. The test reading immediately shows what the area gives.
lieux.affiner: %lld results: refine the search to see more.
lieux.filtrer: Filter by name, area or label
maj.alerte.detail: Synfus restarts; macOS will ask for the permissions again.
maj.autorisations: To grant again after the update
maj.autorisations.aide: Published versions are not signed with a paid Apple certificate: macOS recognises Synfus by its binary's fingerprint, which changes with every version, so the previous version's permissions no longer apply. If a box stays ticked with no effect, remove Synfus from the list (−) and add it back.
maj.echec.ecriture: Unable to install. The app cannot replace itself here.
maj.verifier.aide: Daily, among the versions published on GitHub. A new version is offered here and in the menu; it is only installed on request.
menu.aucunPersoEquipe: No character from this team connected
menu.recentrer: Recenter the bar and the panels
ouTrouver.aide.objet: Where to find this item: the monsters that drop it, its recipe
ouTrouver.rien: Neither dropped by a monster nor crafted.
palette.almanax.sanctuaire.aide: Copy the route to the Almanax Sanctuary, zaap included, to hand in the offering
palette.cmd.invite: The whole team on one line, or one character
palette.cmd.pnj: An NPC located by quests, nearest first
palette.cmd.quete: A quest: the resources to gather and its objectives, with their route
palette.cmd.travel: A place (bank, market, smithmagic…), through the nearest zaap
palette.cmd.zaap: The zaap by name, area or label
palette.depuis.aide: Distances and routes start from this character: the last one read in front.
palette.ici.pasEncore: Position not read yet: go back to the game for a moment, the front character is read every second.
palette.ici.sansPosition: Character position unknown: turn on position reading (Settings › Screen reading).
palette.origine.autoriser.aide: Synfus is not allowed to record the screen, which reading the character's position requires.
palette.origine.inconnue.aide: Read the position of the character in front now.
palette.origine.lire.aide: Position reading is off: distances and routes have no starting point. Opens Settings › Screen reading.
palette.reglages.filtrer: Filter by name, area, label or coordinates
palette.reglages.lieux.aide: A bank, a workshop, a dungeon… is labelled (⌘E) or made a favorite (⌘D) from the palette, or with a right-click on the result.
palette.reglages.quetes.aide: Quests, their objectives and resources, and the position of the NPCs they mention: downloaded from api.dofusdb.fr the first time the palette opens, then every 30 days.
palette.reglages.tri.aide: Auto sorts by match, favorites, habits, then distance. ⌘T changes it in the palette.
palette.tri.aide: Result order: auto, distance, A → Z or type (⌘T)
persos.acheverGeles.aide: A client that freezes while closing stays alive without any window. Synfus probes it and, silent three times in a row (~15 s), force quits it — whether the close came from Synfus or from the game. Kills are logged in Diagnostics.
persos.equipes.aide: Up to four teams, composed here or by dragging a chip onto the row that appears under the bar — onto “+” to create one, onto “All” to leave. The active team restricts the bar, ⌘1…⌘n, next/previous, arranging and the overview; the other characters stay under “All”. Synfus always starts on “All”.
persos.ordre.aide: The order decides slot numbering. Characters not connected are skipped: keep as many as you like. Drag a row, or use the arrows.
persos.oublierHorsLigne.detail: The shortcuts of the characters after them shift.
persos.retirer.detail: The shortcuts of the characters after it shift.
pnj.aide: NPCs located by quests. DofusDB doesn't say whether they're just passing by: the most cited spot comes first.
quete.aFaire.aide: Still to do according to the front character's in-game quest tracker.
quete.aucune.aide: Return on a quest in the palette, or Settings → Quests.
quete.copierNom: Copy the name, for the market
quete.copierTrajet: Copy the route, zaap included, and mark the objective in progress
quete.copierTrajetMonstre: Copy the route to the monster's nearest haunt, zaap included, and mark the objective in progress
quete.guide: Guide on Dofus pour les noobs
quete.nonOuvert.aide: The front character's in-game quest tracker doesn't show it: it opens later in this step — or it's already done, out of order.
quete.persos:
%lld characters at this step according to their game quest tracker:
%@
quete.persos.un:
%lld character at this step according to their game quest tracker:
%@
quete.suggestion.aide: Your character is on this map: click the check mark to complete the objective.
quete.suggestion.combat.aide: A fight just ended on this map: click the check mark to complete the objective.
quete.suivi.coches: %lld objectives checked off from the tracker
quete.suivi.coches.un: %lld objective checked off from the tracker
quete.suivi.rien: No quest recognised in the game tracker.
quete.terminee.aide: It left the game's quest tracker since the previous reading: click to unpin it.
quete.tournee.aide: These objectives are open together in the game's quest tracker, to do in any order: numbered in the shortest order from your character, zaaps included.
quetes.aide: A quest opens in a transparent panel above the game: resources and routes in one click.
quetes.cocherSuivi.aide: When the game's quest tracker is read, the objectives before the first one it shows are checked off (a click unchecks them), and unchecked again if it shows them open — never one you checked yourself. The ones it shows are highlighted.
quetes.compact.aide: Smaller text and tighter lines: the panel hides less of the game.
quetes.consigne.aide: The paragraph under the step title, before the objectives.
quetes.maj.suspecte: DofusDB only returned %lld quests, the current ones are kept.
quetes.masquerObjets.aide: From the resources to gather: they can't be bought, an NPC hands them over or you pick them up on the way.
quetes.vignettes.aide: A small map view next to each objective. Hovering an objective always shows it large.
raccourci.enregistrer.aide: Click, then press the combination. A global shortcut needs at least one modifier.
raccourci.pressez.aide: Press the combination, or Esc to cancel.
raccourcis.aide: Global shortcuts: they work even when Dofus is in front.
raccourcis.allerAUnPerso.aide: One shortcut per connected character, in the order of the Characters tab; characters not connected are skipped.
raccourcis.attention.aide: Detected from the icon bouncing in the Dock, the only signal an app can send outward; Synfus reads nothing from the game itself.
raccourcis.attention.bascule: Turn automatic switching on or off
raccourcis.conflit: This combination is already assigned to another action: the system keeps only one.
raccourcis.enchainer.aide: Hold the key, click in the game: the click goes through normally, then Synfus switches to the next character — like “Next character” on the keyboard. A click without the key stays a click. You still click once per character; only the window switch is automatic. Synfus sends and replays no click.
raccourcis.enchainer.clicsCaptes.aide: If it stays at zero after clicking in the game, macOS is not delivering the events: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring.
raccourcis.enchainer.touche.aide: The game receives the click with the key on it, Synfus does not strip it. fn is the only one the game ignores; ⇧ and ⌥ mean something in Dofus, ⌃-click is a right click for macOS, and a ⌘-click no longer talks to NPCs. If releasing fn opens the emoji picker, set “Press 🌐 key to” to “Do Nothing” in System Settings → Keyboard.
raccourcis.equipeSuivante.aide: Cycles: all characters, team 1, team 2… then all. Teams are composed in the Characters tab or by dragging a chip onto the second row of the bar.
raccourcis.invitation.aide: Puts “/invite Name” on the clipboard, one character per press, cycling over the active team. The leader is the character in front at the first press, and stays so until the end of the round — even if auto-switch changes windows meanwhile. Paste it in the chat (⌘V ↩): Synfus sends nothing to the game.
raccourcis.invitation.format.aide: %nom is replaced by the character's name, as the game shows it in the window title. Right-clicking a chip copies that character's invitation.
raccourcis.invitation.toutes.aide: Puts "/invite A; /invite B; …" in the clipboard: the whole active team except the character in front, on one line. The game chains the commands: a single paste in the chat (⌘V ↩). Synfus sends nothing to the game.
raccourcis.inviter.aide: Synfus sends no event: it composes the command, you paste it. One gesture per guest, like one click per character.
raccourcis.lancerSession.aide: The morning gesture: arranges with the last layout, then switches to character 1.
raccourcis.palette.aide: Zaaps, places (bank, market, smithmagic…), quests, NPCs, monsters, items, game commands, variables, characters: type, Return copies, ⌘V pastes in the chat. / for commands, % for variables, Tab to filter, ⌘T to sort, ⌘E to label, ⌘D for a favorite, Esc to clear.
raccourcis.ranger.aide: Replays the last layout used — side by side, grid, one large + thumbnails, stacked — chosen from the bar button, the menu bar or the right click. No default: your call.
raccourcis.refuse: macOS refused this combination: another app already holds it.
raccourcis.retablir.detail: Your custom shortcuts are replaced by the defaults.
raccourcis.signalerBascule: Blink the character on each switch
raccourcis.signalerBascule.aide: Whenever Synfus switches character — shortcut, click chaining, auto-switch — its chip blinks in the bar for a second and a half.
raccourcis.voirTous.aide: Previews stay visible as long as the combination is held. It must include a modifier, and requires the screen recording permission.
rangement.raison.autreBureau: on another desktop — switch to it then arrange again
rangement.raison.sansEcran: no screen to place it on
stats.partager.aide: Once a day: the counters on this page, the number of characters (never their names), the settings in use, the language, the Synfus and macOS versions, and an identifier hashed from this Mac that reveals nothing about it. Nothing from the game: no name, server, position or text read. Also sent: the crash, hang, and excessive CPU or disk-write reports macOS hands to Synfus, which hold Synfus call stacks. Turning sharing off keeps the counts on this Mac.
trajet.copier.horsDesDouze: Copy the /travel: outside the World of Twelve, no Amakna zaap
vuesCartes.aide: As thumbnails in the palette, the lists and the quest panel, enlarged on hover; behind each zaap. Downloaded from DofusDB on first display and kept in the caches.
zaap.ajout.aide: For a zaap the list doesn't know yet: it counts as a World of Twelve zaap. A zaap already listed is checked in the list.
zaap.auto.aide: Synfus looks at every new copy, from any app, and only touches a "/travel x,y" text. Passwords marked as secret are never read. macOS may ask once whether Synfus can read the clipboard.
zaap.duJeu.aide: The one the game ties to the target sub-area, even if farther: autopilot knows the shortcuts and the cliffs. It only gives way when it lies in another region and a zaap of the target region saves at least %lld more maps. Off: the closest through neighbouring sub-areas.
zaap.gain.aide: Below that, the /travel is left as is.
zaap.intercalees.aide: Inserted between /zaap and /travel, separated by “;”. Right after the zaap, the game sometimes ignores /travel while the map loads; a harmless command such as /a gives it time. Empty: nothing is added.
zaap.liste.aide: Uncheck a zaap so it is never suggested. Those marked "other map" (Incarnam, Canopy, Harebourg, Crocuzko) have coordinates that overlap the World of Twelve, where the game looks up their /zaap and rejects it: unchecked by default.
zaap.maj.aide: Downloads the zaap list from api.dofusdb.fr — Synfus also does it by itself at launch when the list is more than 30 days old. Your choices, additions and favourites are kept.
zaap.raccourci.aide: Rewrites the clipboard's /travel as "/zaap x,y ; /travel a,b" when the zaap saves enough maps. Beeps when nothing changes. Paste it in the chat (⌘V ↩): Synfus sends nothing to the game.
zaap.reecriture.aide: When the copied /travel targets a map far from you, Synfus prefixes it with "/zaap x,y ;" in the clipboard: the zaap the game ties to the target sub-area, or the closest one through neighbouring sub-areas when the game names none, or names one in another region while a zaap of the target region saves at least %lld more maps. An NPC or place picked in Synfus is located by its sub-area (Otomai's Canopy is not the jungle below). Only a "/travel x,y" text is looked at: anything else is left untouched. Your position is the one OCR reads on the last character in front.
